# Tracker rollout — decision deck

## Opening
- [cover] Tracker rollout: approve 180k to cut request turnaround by two thirds
  - body: Cover. Deck title, the decision requested, meeting date placeholder, presenter placeholder.
  - visual: Cover slide per the style's frame.
  - evidence: brief.md, Message.
- [summary] The pilot proved a 3x faster turnaround; full rollout pays back in 14 months
  - body: Executive summary in three points: what the pilot showed, what the rollout costs and returns, what we ask today.
  - visual: Three-point summary, the style's own arrangement for a summary slide.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts.

## The problem
- [problem-numbers] Requests spread over 14 spreadsheets take 6.2 days and one in eleven is lost
  - body: Today's state in numbers: 14 spreadsheets, 5 departments, median 6.2 days, 31% over 10 days, 9% lost.
  - visual: Big-number slide with four or five metrics; the 9% lost is the emphasised one.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Today).
- [before-after] The pilot cut turnaround from 6.2 to 2.1 days and lost requests to zero
  - body: Before vs after the pilot across the same four measures: turnaround, over-10-days share, lost share, satisfaction score.
  - visual: Before / after comparison, two columns or paired values, deltas visible.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Today, Pilot).

## The plan
- [process] Each department switches over in four weeks: configure, migrate, train, switch
  - body: The repeatable four-step onboarding process every department goes through.
  - visual: Four-step horizontal process flow with a short description under each step.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Rollout plan).
- [phases] Three phases bring all five departments onto Tracker by the end of Q2
  - body: Phase 1 Support done, Phase 2 Finance and HR in Q1, Phase 3 Operations and Sales in Q2. Show which departments belong to which phase and the timing.
  - visual: Timeline or roadmap with three phases; departments grouped under each.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Rollout plan).
- [cycle] Tracker closes the loop: every request is logged, routed, resolved and reviewed
  - body: The request lifecycle as a cycle — logged, routed, resolved, reviewed — and why the review step is what stops requests getting lost.
  - visual: Four-node cycle diagram with one sentence per node.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Today: lost requests; Pilot: 0 lost).

## The case
- [cost-table] Year-one cost is 180k, split across licences, migration and training
  - body: Cost breakdown table: three line items with amounts and a total; a note column on what each covers.
  - visual: Table, three rows plus total row, four columns.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Cost).
- [payback-chart] Benefits overtake cost in month 14 and reach +345k net over three years
  - body: Cost versus benefit by year: year one 180k cost against 155k benefit, years two and three 210k benefit each. State the 14-month payback and the three-year net.
  - visual: Bar chart, cost vs benefit for three years, with the payback point called out.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Cost, Benefit, Payback).
- [risks-and-ask] Two known risks are mitigated; we ask for approval of 180k and a Q1 start
  - body: Text-heavy closing: the two risks and their mitigations as short paragraphs, then the decision requested, stated plainly.
  - visual: Two short paragraphs for risks, then the ask as the closing statement in the style's closing convention.
  - evidence: brief.md, Facts (Risks, Decision requested).
